<action type="say">
Understood—since the order shows as delivered but you don’t have it and you’ve checked your mailroom and front desk, this is now a “missing package after delivery” situation.

Here are the usual next steps you should take, in order:

1) Double-check delivery details  
- Look at your order confirmation/shipping email for:
  - Exact shipping address
  - The **carrier** (UPS/USPS/FedEx/Amazon/etc.) and **tracking number**
- If you can, pull up the tracking page and check:
  - The **time and date** marked as delivered
  - The **location note** (e.g., “left at front door,” “parcel locker,” “mailroom,” “reception,” “garage,” etc.)

2) Check a few additional spots  
Even if you’ve checked the mailroom/front desk:
- Any package lockers or building package room
- With neighbors or co-workers in adjacent offices/classrooms
- Any alternate campus mailrooms if that applies to your school

3) Start a carrier trace / missing-package investigation  
Once you have the carrier and tracking number:
- Go to the carrier’s website and start a **“missing package”** or **“package not received”** claim.
- Or call them and say: “Tracking shows delivered, but I did not receive the package. Please start a trace.”  
  - Have: tracking number, your name, full address, and delivery date from the tracking page.

4) Contact the merchant with specific info  
Reach out to the store where you bought the headphones (their support chat/email/phone) and include:
- Order ID: **ODR-104582**
- Your name and email: **jordan.miles@mpls.k12.mn.us**
- Shipping ZIP: **55406**
- A short summary, for example:
  - “Tracking shows delivered on [date/time] by [carrier] to [location note], but I did not receive it. I’ve checked mailroom/front desk and neighbors. Please assist with a replacement or refund and advise next steps.”

Most merchants will:
- Ask you to wait while the carrier completes their trace (often 1–8 business days), and then
- Either send a **replacement** or **issue a refund** if the carrier confirms loss/theft.

If you paste in the **tracking number and carrier** here, I can help you:
- Interpret the tracking events
- Draft an exact message you can send to the merchant and, if needed, to the carrier as well.</action>
